note: Canonical data for tool_registry.py. Each script's own --help is the contract of record; this file is the router. `lanes` carries one object per invocation site in the lane SKILL.md files: {lane, phase, step, template, gate}. `template` is the invocation verbatim, placeholders untouched - it is the only copy.

tools.name: check_acceptance_suite
tools.description: Decides whether a feature's acceptance matrix is well-formed, or was actually run to green, for the build, verify and shipping gates.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = the JSON names the defect; exit 2 = usage or an unparseable matrix - re-delegate to Alex quoting the exact arrays under the same 2-round bound.
Exit 1 = BLOCK: a failure here is a regression since build; exit 2 = a structural defect or a nonexistent `--changed-files` path, routed back to Alex (matrix) or Quinn (results).
Exit 0 is required before Phase 2; on exit 1/2 fix the named arrays and re-run under the 2-round bound, then halt and surface.
Results or capture defects (`missing_results`, `unevidenced_manual`, an unreadable results file) are a delta-only follow-up to Quinn; a matrix defect re-opens Phase 1 and consumes none of her rounds.

tools.name: check_agent_originality
tools.description: Flags near-duplicate agent personas or methodology skills by entity-neutralized shingle overlap, for the agent-audit DRY metric.

tools.name: check_agent_report
tools.description: Decides whether a durable agent report backs its Pass verdict with captured, evidenced check lines and zero Critical findings.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = BLOCK: the JSON names the cause, routed into the step 4 remediation cycle exactly as a Critical finding; exit 2 = a structurally non-conforming report, back to Cipher.
A report or capture defect is a delta-only follow-up to Cipher under the 2-round bound; a confirmed vulnerability is a finding carried to Phase 4, never a loop.
Step 2 re-pointed at Ward's report, same routing; Ward not delegated means no rows for it to gate, so it does not run.
Route per the default exit-code convention; on exit 1 the JSON body names the failing, blocked, unrun and unevidenced items and Critical findings in Vera's report.
Route per the default exit-code convention; on exit 1 the JSON body names the failing, blocked, unrun and unevidenced items and Critical findings in Cipher's report.
Exit 2 = an artifact defect routed back to this same Dep; exit 1, or a `**Verdict:** Fail`, is a live production defect - take the rollback decision and HALT for the user.

tools.name: check_always_on
tools.description: Lints the session-start always-on index for missing lane rows, over-long cells, dangling paths and broken rule owners.

tools.name: check_attack_matrix
tools.description: Decides whether a security attack matrix is well-formed, or whether its rows were probed and evidenced, for the secure lane.

lanes.gate: Exit 0 is required before Phase 2; on exit 1/2 fix the named rows and re-run under the 2-round bound, then halt and surface.
A matrix defect re-opens Phase 1 with the user rather than routing to Cipher, and consumes none of his rounds.

tools.name: check_batch_close
tools.description: Decides whether every bug in a bugfix batch is terminal, committed, worktree-removed and recorded in the batch's Final table.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = BLOCK and the JSON names the open bug, the leftover worktree, the broken chain or the table mismatch - fix it and re-run; never hand-close a batch this gate has not PASSed.

tools.name: check_blockers
tools.description: Decides whether any blocker in the orchestrator state still stands for this milestone at or above a severity floor.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = standing blockers - HALT and list them from the JSON stdout.

tools.name: check_bugfix_intake
tools.description: Decides whether a bug report is complete, non-placeholder and re-runnable before any delegation in the bugfix lane happens.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = BLOCK: fix the named section, placeholder or unanswered enum with the user and re-run; exit 2 = not a bug report; no delegation until this exits 0.

tools.name: check_commit_gate
tools.description: Decides whether a milestone may be committed, and performs the commit, from its review verdict, blockers, evidence and ledger.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_commit_gate.py --review-report {report-root}/review-report.md --state {state-file} --milestone "{bug-slug}" --changed-files <the builder's paths> --verify-tree --require-files-reviewed --max-changed-files 5 --waiver {bugfix-root}/rca.md --require-ledger-gates check_bugfix_intake.py,check_red_green.py,check_handoff.py,check_test_authenticity.py --require-run-log {bugfix-root}/run-log.jsonl --require-agents quinn,luna,<the builder(s) Phase 3 delegated> --ledger {bugfix-root}/gates.jsonl --repo <the target repo root — REQUIRED whenever the invocation's cwd is not that repo> [--docs-root <the shared .docs/ root, only if it is not --repo/.docs>] --commit --message "<the commit message>"
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = BLOCK and the JSON names the stale verdict, standing blocker, standing Critical/Important finding, unreviewed file, tree mismatch, size overrun or unbacked sibling gate; exit 2 = non-conforming report, back to Luna.

tools.name: check_coverage
tools.description: Decides whether every Must-Have requirement is covered by plan tasks, evidenced passing tests, or a filed design supersession.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = one of the two gating arrays is non-empty, `uncovered` and/or `lint_failures`; exit 2 = the artifact failed its structural contract - re-delegate to Alex quoting the exact entries.
This is the supersession-annotation lint, not full FR-to-design coverage: fix every reported `lint_failures` entry before the adversarial pass.
Exit 1 = one of the two gating arrays is non-empty, `uncovered` and/or `lint_failures`; exit 2 = the artifact failed its structural contract - re-delegate to Alex quoting the exact arrays.
Exit 1 = the `uncovered` array lists the Must-Have gaps; exit 2 = the artifact failed its structural contract; either way BLOCK and route back to `/bgpdd-build` Phase 2.

tools.name: check_dependency_tables
tools.description: Decides whether every agent's Methodology Dependencies table resolves to real files, carries the guard wording, and fills each When cell.

tools.name: check_frontmatter
tools.description: Decides whether every agent and skill frontmatter block parses and carries its required keys, so nothing silently fails to register.

tools.name: check_handoff
tools.description: Decides whether an agent's handoff block satisfies that persona's contract: required elements, real paths, honest status, categorised blockers.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <that file> --persona <quinn|mason|nova|luna> --repo . [--repo <dir> ...] --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched that delegation> --ledger {bugfix-root}/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = the agent's contract was not met: return it to that same agent, counting a round under this lane's 2-round bound.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <that file> --persona <name> --repo . [--repo <dir> ...] --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched that delegation> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = the agent's contract was not met - back to that agent, counting the round its own phase counts.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <that file> --persona <iris|scout|echo> --repo . [--repo <dir> ...] --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched that delegation> --ledger .docs/summary/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = the agent's contract was not met: return it to that same agent, subject to the error-recovery bound in section 2.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <that file> --persona <alex|scout> --repo . [--repo <dir> ...] --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched the delegation> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = his contract was not met - back to Alex under section 2's 2-round bound, not on to the coverage gate.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <that file> --persona <rex|aria|alex> --repo . [--repo <dir> ...] --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched that delegation> --milestone "<phase>" --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = the agent's contract was not met - return to that same agent, counting the round its own loop's bound counts; exit 2 = usage or an artifact defect - fix the invocation or the artifact, not the agent.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <that file> --persona cipher --repo . --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched him> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = a delta-only follow-up under section 2's bound, not a Phase 3 gate run.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = Cipher's contract was not met - back to him, counting the round under the Fix-routing bound.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <Dep's saved handoff> --persona dep --repo . --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched Stage 2> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = Dep's contract was not met - back to him, counting the round under the Fix-routing bound.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <her saved handoff> --persona quinn --repo . --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched this fresh delegation> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = back to her, counting the round under this gate's own bound.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <his saved handoff> --persona dep --repo . --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched this fresh delegation> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = back to him, counting the round under Step 3's fix-and-reverify bound.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <his saved handoff> --persona forge --advisory --repo . --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched this delegation> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = the proposal's contract was not met - do not HALT for approval on it; return to Forge for a conforming proposal.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <his saved handoff> --persona forge --repo . --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched the apply delegation> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = back to Forge for a conforming `<changed_skills>` list.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_handoff.py --handoff <that file> --persona quinn --repo . [--repo <dir> ...] --since <the sha HEAD held when you launched her> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = a delta-only follow-up under section 2's bound, not a Phase 3 gate run.

tools.name: check_ledger
tools.description: Decides whether a gate ledger's hash chain is intact, naming the first broken link, before any verdict is read out of it.

lanes.gate: A non-zero exit means that bug's chain is broken, so its `check_commit_gate.py` PASS cannot be trusted and the merge precondition does not hold.

tools.name: check_openapi_diff
tools.description: Decides whether a head OpenAPI document breaks the published contract, for the agent evolving an API and for the shipping gate.
tools.reason: api-contract-evolution/SKILL.md step 5 and its Verification section: the agent that just changed the contract document runs the diff on its OWN output before handing it back. bgpdd-shipping runs the epic-wide diff itself.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_openapi_diff.py --base <that path> --head <the working doc> --milestone "<the epic or feature name>" --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Exit 1 = BLOCK per `api-contract-evolution`; a break authorized by a plan task re-runs with `--allow-breaking "<the task id and reason>"`; exit 2 routes per the default convention.

tools.name: check_quick_close
tools.description: Decides whether a quick-lane change was declared, checked after the edit, small, froze no test, and may now be committed.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = BLOCK and `problem_codes` names the term - `size_bound_exceeded` is unfixable here because the bound is the lane; exit 2 = artifact or environment defect, never hand-edited to pass.

tools.name: check_red_green
tools.description: Decides whether a RED capture and its GREEN captures constitute a real before/after proof of one bugfix.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = BLOCK and the JSON names the failing term; `--no-flaky-pass` is always on here, so a GREEN that only passed on a retry is the false-fixed case this lane exists to catch.

tools.name: check_redelegation
tools.description: Decides whether an agent may be re-delegated on a unit, or whether the lane must halt for the user instead.

tools.name: check_runtime_evidence
tools.description: Decides whether a report's runtime-evidence citations are real out-of-process observations: provenance, transport, freshness, required response keys.

lanes.gate: A non-zero exit means the runtime claim is unbacked: an in-process test can fail this bug but never prove it fixed, and neither gate substitutes for the other.
A stale or non-conforming capture is a delta-only follow-up to whoever owns it; never loosen or invent a `--surface`/`--forbid-host` value the Phase 1 preamble does not carry.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_runtime_evidence.py --report .docs/{project-name}/implementation/verification-report.md --milestone "<the epic or feature name Vera scoped her report to>" --changed-files <the epic's changed-files union> --repo . --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl [--require-key <k> ...] [--forbid-host <pattern> ...] [--require-openapi-reachable]
lanes.gate: Exit 0 = at least one fresh out-of-process capture backs Vera's runtime claims; exit 1/2 route per the default convention, and exit 2's producing agent is Vera.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_runtime_evidence.py --report .docs/{project-name}/implementation/post-deploy-report.md --milestone "post-deploy" --changed-files <the epic's changed-files union, the same set Step 3 derived> --repo . --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl [--require-key <k> ...] [--forbid-host <pattern> ...]
lanes.gate: Not redundant on the report gate: exit 2 is an artifact defect back to the same Dep, exit 1 is a live production defect and the rollback decision is the user's.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/check_runtime_evidence.py --report .docs/{project-name}/implementation/test-report.md --milestone "<run title>" --changed-files <Quinn's spec-file union> --repo <target repo root> --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: A field emitted as null is a Phase 1 defect - fix the preamble with the user, re-lint, re-emit; never fill it in by hand.

tools.name: check_runtime_recipe
tools.description: Decides whether the runtime-environment recipe names a real service start command and readiness check, or a reasoned skip.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 means the recipe names no start command, no readiness check, or is missing a manifest block - fix it with the user now, while they are still here to ask.

tools.name: check_section_anchors
tools.description: Decides whether every section-anchor citation under agents and skills resolves to a real heading or file.

tools.name: check_ship_decision
tools.description: Decides whether a ship decision is GO, rehearsed and baselined, for the shipping lane's final gate.

lanes.gate: Exit 0 = prep GO present; exit 1 = NO-GO or incomplete decision, HALT; exit 2 = structural or missing.
The resume branch's structural check only: exit 1/2 = malformed decision, HALT; do NOT add `--require-go` here, it would block re-entry to the only stage that can resolve a NO-GO.
Exit 1/2 = BLOCK; on a `rehearsal_*` or `baseline_*` problem code the route is back to Dep, because no re-wording of the decision document closes it.

tools.name: check_test_authenticity
tools.description: Decides whether a changed test tests the product or only itself: inline reimplementation, source eval, synthetic DOM, no production import.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = back to Quinn (Phase 1), counts as a round; exit 2 = artifact defect - a RED that does not exercise production code is not a reproduction.
Exit 1 = the one round this lane allows - fix and re-run; exit 2 = artifact defect; skipping it makes the close gate refuse with `test_authenticity_gate_missing`.
Exit 1 = a delta-only follow-up to Quinn under section 2's 2-round bound; exit 2 = artifact defect.

tools.name: check_tier1_provenance
tools.description: Decides whether every Tier-1 discovery artifact carries a resolvable date-and-sha provenance stamp per in-scope repo, optionally gating drift.

lanes.gate: Drift warns, never halts: relay the artifact, its stamped sha and current HEAD, and pass `--allow-drift "<reason>"` only on the user's explicit word, recording it.

Exit 1 means Iris's `context.md` header is unstamped, undated, or names a sha that resolves to nothing - return it to her rather than stamping it yourself; `tier1_repo_dropped` means a repo the backup recorded is gone from the new file.
Exit 1 returns to Echo; do not stamp her artifact for her.
Drift warns, never halts: relay the artifact, its stamped sha and current HEAD, and let the user choose between planning against this map and re-running `/bgpdd-discovery`.
Drift warns, never halts: relay the artifact, its stamped sha and current HEAD, and let the user decide whether to plan against this map or re-run `/bgpdd-discovery` first.
Drift warns, never halts: relay the named artifact, its stamped sha and current HEAD, and pass `--allow-drift "<their reason>"` only on the user's explicit word.
Drift warns, never halts: a stale baseline is a stale matrix, so the user decides before you transcribe.

tools.name: detect_stack
tools.description: Reports evidence-backed technology stacks for a repository, and which methodology skills, check commands and test globs follow from them.

lanes.gate: Its `skills` array is the resolved stack list injected into every builder, Quinn and Luna brief when Tier 1 has none; without it the stack skills are decided by prose.
An empty detection supports treating the repo as greenfield, but is not itself the fit-check answer.
Its block is the mechanical floor a stack-specific skill's dependency row checks against; Iris may add a stack on her own evidence but never remove a detected one.
Propose, never adopt, its defaults: the user confirms or replaces the `How verified` command and the `test_path_globs` Phase 3 passes as `--frozen`, never you silently.

tools.name: diff_findings
tools.description: Classifies a security report's findings across a rescan as RESOLVED, PERSISTENT or NEW, by fingerprint rather than position.

lanes.gate: A NEW finding is treated as a Phase 3 report-gate failure - the live report alone cannot tell a fixed finding from a standing one.

tools.name: guard_action
tools.description: PreToolUse hook that denies a tool call violating one of eight pipeline restraints; the model never invokes it directly.

tools.name: mark_milestone
tools.description: Appends or removes a milestone's completion marker in the plan, only when gates, commit and game tape back the claim.

lanes.gate: It refuses the `[x]` without a commit naming the milestone, a PASS `check_commit_gate.py` entry in an intact-chain ledger, and a conforming Phase 6 checkpoint - completion is recorded only here, never by hand.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/mark_milestone.py --plan .docs/{project-name}/implementation/plan.md --reopen "<the milestone the finding affects>" --evidence <the shipping report or capture the finding came from> --reason "<the gate that produced it>" --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Without the reopen every milestone is `[x]`, `next_milestone.py` returns `DONE`, and build's re-entry has nothing pending to route to.

tools.name: next_bugfix_route
tools.description: Derives the bugfix lane's FAST, FULL or PLAN route from the bug report, its RED capture and the RCA.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 = `INCOMPLETE` (rca.md lacks a routing field) or `BLOCKED` (`red_command_mismatch`/`red_sidecar_missing`); exit 2 = `--red` missing when required, or the intake PASS absent or no longer matching the report's bytes.

tools.name: next_milestone
tools.description: Derives the next milestone to build from the plan, detects a stale cursor, and can emit the runtime gate's arguments.

lanes.gate: The plan is the single authority on what to build next: on `stale: true` reset the cursor and tell the user, and treat any `unbacked_complete` entry as a state defect.
Result `MIXED` (exit 1), including an `UNTAGGED` milestone treated as `MIXED`, is a planning defect - halt and surface it, do not improvise a split.

Result `DONE` proceeds; any other result HALTs - `NEXT` means build is unfinished, `MIXED`/`UNTAGGED` means the plan is malformed, and a stale-cursor verdict means unchecked work sits behind the stored cursor.

tools.name: pipeline_driver
tools.description: Emits the one next mandatory action for a bugfix, quick or batch lane, with its exact flags.

lanes.gate: Exit 1 means a gate for the current phase has not passed - run that gate, never the next phase (exit 3 = the lane is closed; exit 2 = the root or route is mis-resolved).
It prints the next open bug's own driver invocation, or the close gate, or - at exit 3 - that the batch is complete; deciding what to do next without it is recalling a phase rather than emitting it.
Each bug's own phase inside its worktree stays driven by this invocation; the batch driver names it rather than substituting for it.
Exit 1 means the current phase's gate has not passed - run that gate, never the next phase (exit 3 = closed and committed).

tools.name: record_capture
tools.description: Records a PNG's provenance sidecar naming the URL the browser had open, so a mockup render stops looking real.

tools.name: record_run
tools.description: Appends one run-telemetry record per delegation, gate, phase or note, refusing a missing model, missing tokens, a duplicate, or an inverted tier.

lanes.gate: `--model` is mandatory on a delegation record - exit 2 without it - and so is a token measurement; Phase 5's `--require-run-log`/`--require-agents` refuse the commit without these records.
`--model <tier>` is mandatory on a delegation record - exit 2 without it - and a token measurement is equally mandatory.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/record_run.py --log .docs/summary/run-log.jsonl --pipeline bgpdd-discovery --phase "<phase>" --event delegation --agent <iris|scout|echo> --model <tier> --unit "<{feature}, or the {api} for a Scout>" …
lanes.gate: `--model` is mandatory on a delegation return - exit 2 without it - and this log is what Phase 5's `/bgpdd-learn` offer reads.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/record_run.py --log .docs/{project-name}/implementation/run-log.jsonl --pipeline bgpdd-lite --phase "<phase>" --event delegation --agent <name> --model <tier> --unit <the artifact the delegation produced, e.g. plan.md> …
lanes.gate: `--model` is mandatory on a delegation record - exit 2 without it - and a token measurement is equally mandatory.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/record_run.py --log .docs/{project-name}/implementation/run-log.jsonl --pipeline bgpdd-plan --phase "<phase>" --event delegation --agent <name> --model <tier> --unit <the artifact the delegation produced, e.g. requirements.md> …
lanes.gate: `--model` is mandatory on a delegation record - exit 2 without it - and a token measurement is equally mandatory.
`--model` is mandatory, as is a token measurement and `--rounds` on a re-delegation.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/record_run.py --log .docs/{project-name}/implementation/run-log.jsonl --pipeline bgpdd-shipping --phase "<step>" --event delegation --agent <name> --model <tier> --unit "<the epic or feature name — the same token Step 3 passes to --milestone; `post-deploy` for the Step 5.5 Dep>" …
lanes.gate: `--model` is mandatory on a delegation record - exit 2 without it - and these records are what make Step 6.5's whole-epic roll-up true.
`--model` is mandatory on a delegation record - exit 2 without it - and a token measurement is equally mandatory.

tools.name: review_package
tools.description: Renders the diff a reviewer was told to review as one markdown file plus a provenance sidecar.

lanes.gate: Exit 2 = git failed, the diff is empty, every path was excluded, or the reviewable diff exceeds 1500 lines with no `## Size waiver` recorded - never delegate Luna without the package.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/review_package.py --repo . --base HEAD --head WORKTREE --changed-files <the accumulated Phase 1 step 6 list> --out .docs/{project-name}/implementation/review/review-package.md --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl --milestone "<milestone title>" --max-diff-lines 1500 --waiver .docs/{project-name}/implementation/review/size-waiver.md
lanes.gate: Exit 2 = git failed, the diff is empty, every path was excluded, or the reviewable diff exceeds 1500 lines with no `## Size waiver` recorded - never delegate Luna without the package.

reads: <the repo's git history and working tree>

tools.name: run_quiet
tools.description: Runs a command, writes its full output to disk, prints a short report, and optionally writes a runtime-evidence capture.
tools.reason: base-persona.md section Command Timeout Discipline (Anti-Hang): EVERY agent wraps the commands it runs in run_quiet.py --log, and agents/cipher.md and agents/vera.md take each check through --capture. An agent running it is doing its own work properly, not adjudicating it; the gate that reads the capture still runs in the main session.

lanes.gate: No capture means no `{bug-slug}.md.meta.json` sidecar, which is what Phase 4's gate reads; the reproduction command's own non-zero exit is expected here - it is the RED oracle.
Exit 124 with a `TIMEOUT:` header is a harness result to escalate, never recorded as a test FAIL.
Exit 0 is required; non-zero means fix and re-run, the one round this lane allows, and Phase 3 reads the `check.md.meta.json` sidecar a hand-written capture does not have.
Every step's evidence is a fresh capture written this way under `evidence/runtime/`; a capture not produced by it carries no sidecar for the gate to read.
Quinn starts the application and executes the suite through it; a capture not taken with `--capture` carries no sidecar for the Phase 3 gate to read.

reads: <the child command's merged stdout and stderr>

tools.name: summarize_run
tools.description: Summarizes a run log and gate ledger into cost, rounds and fired-versus-rubber-stamped gate counts, optionally as a game-tape block.

lanes.gate: Its pasted block is the telemetry Phase 5's game-tape gate requires; without it `--require-game-tape` fails `no-telemetry`.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/summarize_run.py --run-log <the lane's run log> --ledger <the lane's gate ledger>
lanes.gate: Without its fired-versus-rubber-stamped counts the evidence brief cannot satisfy the Incident Test on any gate proposal Forge makes.
Its block is what Phase 3's game tape pastes; a cost line written from memory is not that block.
Its block goes into Phase 4's game tape; a cost line written from memory is not that block.
Its block goes into Phase 4's game tape.
Paste the block verbatim and do not narrate cost in prose alongside it; if the run log is absent, say so in one bullet and move on.
Its block goes into Phase 4's game tape.

tools.name: tier1_staleness
tools.description: Reports which Tier-1 discovery docs are stale against their stamped shas, so a refresh re-runs only the affected ones.

lanes.gate: Read-only: it changes no exit code and never re-stamps anything, but without its table "refresh or reuse" is answered from a guess instead of evidence.
Run it whenever the provenance check reports drift and paste its table in place of the bare drift warning - it names WHICH docs the drift actually touches.

tools.name: tool_registry
tools.description: Routes an agent or the Orchestrator to the right pipeline-tools script, and verifies the registry against each script's own --help.

tools.name: update_state
tools.description: The sanctioned read-modify-write path for orchestrator-state.json: cursor, artifacts, blockers, halts and status, gated by evidence.

lanes.gate: Without this write the standalone route has no state file, and Phase 5's commit gate reads the `blockers` ledger this call guarantees.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/update_state.py --state {state-file} --set-status escalated --reason "PLAN route: capability, not a bug" --milestone "{bug-slug}" --ledger {bugfix-root}/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: The PLAN HALT must close the lane before routing, or `guard_action.py`'s frozen-test rule denies the receiving lane's own test-file writes.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/update_state.py --state {state-file} --set-status escalated --reason "blast radius: <one line, cite Luna's finding>" --milestone "{bug-slug}" --ledger {bugfix-root}/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: The blast-radius HALT must close the lane before routing - an open lane blocks the receiving lane's test-file edits under `guard_action.py`'s frozen-test rule.
Exit 1 blocks the write and the tape gate fires (`game-tape-missing|no-section|bullet-count|no-pasted-output|no-telemetry`); on the feature route this flag cannot bind, so read the tape yourself.
Without this write there is no durable record of the bug list, and it sets exactly the fields `check_batch_close.py` and the batch driver read.
An unrecorded root, worktree or status leaves the bug invisible to `check_batch_close.py` and to the batch driver, which read these fields.
Without this re-stamp the epic keeps the `bgpdd-shipping` value that shipping's own fix routing left behind, so the re-entry this whitelist widening exists for never completes.
State is written only through this script, never by hand-editing JSON; the cursor move carries the Phase 6 gate, and exit 1 blocks the write so nothing is persisted.
This write backs the Hydration Phase's `branch` rule and is what `bgpdd-shipping` reads; without it shipping diffs and pushes the wrong ref.
Without this write there is no state file for Phase 3 to update and `/bgpdd-build` has nothing to hydrate.
This updates the artifacts Alex produced without `--init`; a failure leaves `/bgpdd-build` hydrating a state whose `plan` is still null.
A missing capability does not halt planning, but it must be recorded here so the blocker travels to `/bgpdd-build`, where Phase 0 re-checks it.
`--init` and `--set-pipeline bgpdd-plan` are both mandatory: without `--init` the command exits 2 on a fresh run, and `--init` alone writes `pipeline: ""`, which build's hydration whitelist rejects.
If Python is unavailable, HALT and surface the missing interpreter - this JSON is never hand-written.
State is never hand-edited here, and the `--add-blocker` writes for authorization/environment blocks and BLOCKED rows carry `--ledger`.
Nothing else writes the value step 2 and build's re-entry rule both read, so without this stamp step 4's resume branch and that re-entry are unreachable.

lanes.template: python {PLUGIN_ROOT}/pipeline-tools/scripts/update_state.py --state .docs/{project-name}/orchestrator-state.json --add-blocker "<the shipping finding, with the gate that produced it and its evidence path>" --blocker-source shipping --blocker-milestone "<the milestone the finding affects>" --ledger .docs/{project-name}/implementation/gates.jsonl
lanes.gate: Record the finding as a blocker before handing the user the `/bgpdd-build` instruction, and scope it with `--blocker-milestone` - an unscoped entry blocks everything.
State is never hand-edited here, and the `--add-blocker` writes for environment blocks and BLOCKED verifications carry `--ledger`.
